image_description: A close-up, high-contrast image of a cooked Dungeness crab (Cancer magister) positioned centrally against a dark background. The crab is viewed from the ventral side (underside), showing its folded abdomen and the arrangement of its legs and claws. The shell exhibits characteristic reddish-orange hues on the limbs and tips, transitioning to creamy white on the underside and joints. The lighting creates strong specular highlights on the glossy exoskeleton.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The two large chelipeds are prominent at the top of the frame. They are robust, and while symmetry is hard to judge perfectly due to pose, they appear naturally proportioned. The tips show distinct darker reddish/orange pigmentation compared to the white joints.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Claws have smooth outer surface and serrated inner edges.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The outer surfaces of the claws appear smooth. The inner edges (visible where the pincers open slightly) show textural complexity consistent with serrations/teeth, though fine detail is limited by resolution.

artifact_observations.reasoning: Some of the joint connections appear slightly 'mushy' or overly blended rather than having distinct mechanical separation lines typical of arthropod exoskeletons. This is subtle but noticeable upon close inspection of the lower-left legs.

The segmentation of the abdominal plates (pleonites) lacks clear definition. Instead of distinct overlapping plates, the area appears as a somewhat fused, lumpy mass without crisp boundaries between segments.
The tip of the right claw seems to curve inward at an anatomically unlikely angle, potentially indicating slight geometric warping common in AI generation of complex curved objects.
